meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on Owen's zero, Hale, and did anyone speak to him first?
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.
A machine's guess isn't evidence, and Turnitin's own guide says its score shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student. I have it printed in my bag. What else have you got?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.
Okay. What else is there besides the score?

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
11:52 and 11:58, I'll want those times in writing. People draft somewhere else and paste it in, Hale. Does that history show where the words came from?

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.
Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet. As for the line, a seventeen-year-old misremembering Shakespeare is careless, not proof of anything.
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their thesis between an outline and a final draft, Hale. And you haven't answered me on the misquoted line.

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.
Five minutes on the spot with his teacher, and a seventeen-year-old freezes. So you did speak to him first. Where is this going?

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Forty minutes under a clock against a take-home essay isn't a fair comparison. You've laid out five things. What are you actually asking for?

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.
That's 4.4, so in writing, tonight, with the words "nothing on his record" in it. He'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. And it gets marked well before December 1.
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Thursday, then, and marked within two days. Who supervises it, and in which room?
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
We do, once it's in my inbox tonight. Put who's supervising him in that same email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 this Thursday after school, marked within two days, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require all of that in writing, including the name of the person supervising him. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, marked within two days, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record. She still wants all of it in writing tonight, with the supervisor named. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her call.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its times, then answered her pasted-from-elsewhere defence by inviting Owen to show the other document. It was dated, tied to his work, and something she could check.
What cost ground: You led with the checker score and said the zero stands. She can't check a score, and the vendor's own guidance says it shouldn't be the only basis for a penalty.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop. Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the essay's creation between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, a late October night, very close to what she saw. That proves nothing about the essay. It is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open with your apology for entering the zero before calling home, go straight to the version history, and leave the checker score out entirely.
